specification.problem: Implement a quantum oracle U_f|x>|y>=|x>|y xor f(x)> for an arbitrary classical Boolean function f in constant depth, via MBQC equivalence with a circuit model having arbitrary Z rotations and unbounded fan-out. The abstract gives no explicit construction.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful instance: the n-bit OR (disjunction) oracle, with a background-style phase-polynomial form of a Boolean function as the Z-rotation ingredient. The actual constant-depth MBQC construction, its depth bound, and the exact OR implementation are outside scope and not reconstructed.

symbols.domain: positive integer (tiny instance n=2 or 3 assumed)

symbols.meaning: Z-rotation angle for parity of subset S

equations.label: Oracle action
equations.description: Standard definition of a quantum oracle implementing a classical function, with computational basis encoding of x and y.
equations.abstract_quote: any quantum oracle implementing a classical function
equations.justification: The abstract refers to oracles implementing classical functions; the bit-flip form is the standard meaning, not stated explicitly.

equations.label: Phase oracle from bit oracle
equations.description: The bit oracle equals a Hadamard-conjugated diagonal phase oracle on the target qubit.
equations.justification: Standard identity: H Z H = X controlled on f(x).
assumptions: Z-type phase on target qubit controlled by f(x)

equations.label: Walsh expansion of phase
equations.description: Boolean function phase as a combination of parity characters, which relates to Z-rotations on parities computed with fan-out.
equations.justification: Standard Fourier analysis on the Boolean cube; not stated in the abstract.

equations.label: Z rotation on parity
equations.description: Arbitrary Z-axis rotation as the elementary gate, to be applied to qubits holding parities x_S.
equations.abstract_quote: arbitrary rotations along $Z$ axis and unbounded fan-outs are elementary operations
equations.justification: The abstract names arbitrary Z rotations as elementary; the explicit form is standard. The angle schedule is not given and is not invented.

equations.label: Disjunction function
equations.description: Boolean definition of the n-bit OR whose exact constant-depth oracle is the corollary.
equations.abstract_quote: disjunction can be implemented exactly in constant-depth
equations.justification: The OR function is the target of the corollary; the algebraic form is standard background.
assumptions: Construction of the constant-depth circuit is not given

registers.name: x
registers.role: input register in computational basis, qubit i holds x_i

registers.name: anc
registers.role: ancillas for fan-out/parity computation and MBQC resource; count not given

specification.initial_state: |x>|y>|0...0> on computational basis input (or a superposition over x), with ancillas in |0>; assumed.

steps.description: Prepare input and target; the oracle is to be defined by the bit-flip action.
Conjugate the target with Hadamards to reduce to a phase oracle.
Express the phase (-1)^{f(x)} via parities; compute needed parities with unbounded fan-out/CNOT-type operations (specific scheme not given).
Apply Z rotations on parity qubits, uncompute parities; the angle schedule is missing from the abstract. Then the circuit is translated to MBQC through the stated equivalence.
For the OR instance, the target function is eq_5; the exact constant-depth circuit is not reconstructed.

assumptions: Scope chosen by me: OR/phase-polynomial oracle as a tiny instance (n=2 or 3).
Walsh-parity approach is a generic background route and not claimed to be the paper's method.
Constant-depth property, MBQC pattern, and equivalence mapping are not derived.
missing_information: Actual constant-depth construction for arbitrary f
MBQC measurement pattern and feed-forward correction rules
Depth bound and exact OR construction
